source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: The punctuation shot: a complete story beat — entrance, scatter, eruption — in 31 frames on an empty stage. Richard storms in, the family hits the floor, and the scream is a single held pose with micro-variations. Nothing is wasted: one entrance vector, one group reaction, one held accent. Short shots in this production are built like jokes — setup inside 12 frames, payoff held.
notes: Richard enters at frame ~9 on an empty white stage; by f12 the kids are on the floor and the remote is loose — the entrance and the scatter happen inside 12 frames.
The scream pose (arms up, mouth at full stretch) lands at ~f16 and is HELD with small variations to f31: a 31-frame punctuation shot, not a full scene beat.
The background plate does not render in this SWF export (white stage), the same pattern as Sc105 — the layout BG is a separate plate (see backgrounds census).
Production frame counter (001/005/009…) is burned into the export, as across this archive.
